newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo consumer defaults down 4.4 pct in Nov.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo consumer defaults down 4.4 pct in Nov.

text.p: Consumer defaults in Sao Paulo city rose 9.8 percent to 173,097 in November when compared with the same period of 1995, but fell 4.4 percent against October this year, said Sao Paulo Commerce Association (ACSP).
November figures compared with October show consumers and retailers have been cautious ahead of the Christmas season, when sales are traditionally higher, said Emilio Alfieri, economist at ACSP.

Although slightly lower, the consumer defaults, which are measured by the number of reported payment in arrears for over 30 days, do not eliminate the risk of another surge in consumer bankruptcies in the first quarter of next year, Alfieri said.
"It is too early to say how early next year will be because Christmas shopping has just begun. But we would feel more comfortable if consumer defaults had fallen sharply," he said.
Consumers defaults had declined between May and September and resumed rising in October, when defaults totalled 181,116, an increase of 18 percent compared with September.
